quote: So I think that with those trees still there, I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun, for them to be super fully fully beneficial to you.
stewart_read: Rep reaches a hard-DQ-style conclusion from a satellite image alone without asking which side of the roof the trees shade or for what portion of the day — a process gap in how shading DQs should be verified before being delivered to the customer.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been trained that any visible trees near the roof are an automatic DQ signal regardless of orientation, making this a knowledge/training issue rather than a one-off judgment call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask 'which side of the roof gets the most sun, and about how many hours a day' before concluding shading disqualifies the home — the customer's own knowledge of the property is a faster and more accurate data source than a map image.

quote: So, yeah, I really do apologize, but I can get you off our list if you don't get any more calls. Okay?
stewart_read: Rep moves straight from a tentative shading impression ('I think... I don't think') to offering to remove the customer from the list entirely — a disproportionate action given the DQ hasn't actually been verified.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as the rep being conscientious about not wasting the customer's time on a bad lead, but the tentative language just before ('I think that... I don't think') shows the rep is not confident enough in the DQ to be closing the door this fast.
coaching_implication: Separate 'possible shading concern' from 'offering to remove from the list' — the latter should only happen after the rep has actually confirmed orientation and shading duration with the customer, not on a first-glance impression.

quote: Once I once I have that side gets a lot. ... only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
stewart_read: The customer directly volunteers the exact information (which side gets sun, limited/partial shading) that would let the rep re-evaluate the DQ, and the rep does not ask a single follow-up question about it before repeating the same conclusion at 02:20.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that even partial shading on 'a ton of space' was disqualifying regardless of the customer's detail, making this a deliberate (if unstated) technical judgment rather than an oversight.
coaching_implication: When a customer offers specific corrective detail to a DQ, the rep should ask at least one clarifying question (e.g., 'which side is that, and about what time of day does the shade hit?') before restating the same conclusion — otherwise the customer reasonably perceives they weren't heard.

quote: I can reach out to my design team and see if they would be able to do anything. And then if they can, I'll give you a callback, and we could totally get you scheduled. Okay?
stewart_read: The call ends with a conditional, undated callback promise instead of either a resolved DQ or a locked next step — no timeframe, no specific commitment, and no confirmation the customer even wants to be recontacted given the earlier list-removal offer.
coaching_implication: If a DQ needs design-team review, give the customer a concrete timeframe ('I'll have an answer by Friday and call you then') rather than an open-ended 'if they can, I'll call' — this protects the lead and sets a clear expectation.

quote: We've only been renting it for about a little over a year, but, we've owned the home for a long time.
stewart_read: The customer gives an ambiguous ownership statement — renting the current residence for a year but having 'owned the home for a long time' — which directly touches the hard homeowner-status qualifier, and the rep never clarifies whether the customer owns THIS home (the one being evaluated for solar) or a different one.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have interpreted 'owned the home for a long time' as confirming ownership of this specific address and moved on satisfied, but the statement as given is genuinely contradictory and was never resolved either way.
coaching_implication: This is a hard qualifier gap, not a minor rapport miss: the rep should have asked directly 'so is this the home you own, or are you renting this one and own another?' before proceeding — solar cannot be sold to a renter, and this was left unresolved before the DQ conversation even started.
